niche: Psychology & human behavior (biases, habits, social dynamics)

ideas.title: Why You Get Great Ideas in the Shower
ideas.angle: Explains the 'shower effect' where mind-wandering during routine, non-demanding tasks releases dopamine and shifts the brain into the default mode network, unlocking creative epiphanies. Shows fast-paced b-roll of flowing water, city walks, and sudden realizations.

hook.en: Stop trying so hard to think.

keywords: pourquoi bonnes idées sous la douche
ideas.reason: Creativity and overthinking hacks regularly go viral on Shorts because everyone experiences sudden shower insights; recent 2022-2023 cognitive psychology experiments by Zac Irving confirmed the exact mechanics behind mind-wandering and task incubation.
sources: Irving et al. (2022) - 'The Shower Effect: Mind Wandering Facilitates Creative Incubation During Moderately Engaging Activities', Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts
Christoff et al. (2016) - 'Mind-wandering as spontaneous thought', Nature Reviews Neuroscience

ideas.title: Why Big Plates Trick Your Appetite
ideas.angle: Reveals the Delboeuf Illusion, showing how the exact same portion size looks drastically smaller on a larger plate, unconsciously forcing your brain to serve more food and feel hungrier. Visualized with geometric circle contrasts and aerial shots of plated meals.

hook.en: Your plate is controlling your appetite.

ideas.reason: Everyday health and perceptual illusions have exceptionally high shareability and comment rates due to people testing the visual illusion directly on screen in the first 5 seconds.
sources: Delboeuf, F. J. (1865) - 'Note sur certaines illusions d'optique'
Wansink & van Ittersum (2012) - 'Plate Size and Color Suggestibility: The Delboeuf Illusion's Bias on Serving and Eating Behaviour', Journal of Consumer Research

ideas.title: Why Strangers Like You More Than You Think
ideas.angle: Breaks down the 'Liking Gap'—a systematic cognitive bias where people consistently underestimate how much a conversation partner enjoyed talking to them and how positive their first impression was. Uses urban candid pedestrian interactions and coffee shop footage.

hook.en: They liked you more than you think.
hook.fr: Ils t'ont apprécié bien plus que prévu.

ideas.reason: Social anxiety and self-doubt content are evergreen drivers of high engagement and saves on Shorts; this provides instant emotional relief backed by solid empirical data from Boothby et al.
sources: Boothby et al. (2018) - 'The Liking Gap in Conversations: Do People Like Us More Than We Think?', Psychological Science
Reagan et al. (2021) - 'The Liking Gap Over Time', Journal of Experimental Social Psychology
